name: LiveWorld
use_label: Browse the world's live cams on a globe
one_liner: Every 24/7 YouTube live camera on one spinning globe you can browse.

text.why: Live cameras on cities, beaches and harbours are everywhere but scattered. LiveWorld gathers them on a globe so you can spin to a region and open a feed.
text.take: No install, no login — one tab shows you what the world looks like right now.
build: Cameras sit on a satellite-imagery globe as numbered clusters, with search by camera, city or country, a random jump (the dice), saved cameras, submissions and ambient music. Per the site, one person built it and keeps 2,418 cameras online.

who.role: Anyone wanting a view of another city on a break, or a preview of a place before travelling.

start.text: Open liveworld.info and spin the globe, or press the dice for a random camera.

caveat: Per the site's cookie notice, it shows a few ads. The feeds are YouTube live streams, so a camera disappears when its stream stops. Source availability and licence could not be confirmed.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.

images.alt: LiveWorld's globe: yellow clusters counting cameras around Korea and Japan, with music, menu, saved and submit buttons below.

notes: This file was produced by the same build, from the same data, as the tesign.com item page. The text is editorial; the numbers are stored observations.
null in the JSON means not observed — never zero. The Markdown writes [unconfirmed] for it.

Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.
